microtheory.name: audio_music_foundation
microtheory.definition: The substrate's foundational vocabulary for sound and music — basic acoustic + musical concepts that ground its existing audio cortices (auditory_cortex, cochlear_nucleus, phonology, speech_science) and provide the explanatory layer for what those mechanisms compute on. Spans physical (waveform, frequency, amplitude), perceptual (pitch, timbre, loudness), and musical (melody, harmony, rhythm) levels. Substrate analogue: the input domain its existing speech + auditory pipelines process.

concepts.name: sound
concepts.definition: Mechanical wave propagating through a medium. Compression + rarefaction of particles. Substrate analogue: the input modality of its auditory pipeline.

concepts.name: waveform
concepts.definition: Time-domain representation of sound — pressure vs time. Substrate analogue: the raw audio buffer at the input of cochlear processing.

concepts.name: frequency
concepts.definition: Number of cycles per second; Hz. Determines pitch. Human range ~20Hz-20kHz. Substrate analogue: the axis of substrate's tonotopic gammatone filterbank.

concepts.name: amplitude
concepts.definition: Magnitude of pressure variation. Determines loudness. Logarithmic perception. Substrate analogue: power output of each gammatone channel.

concepts.name: phase
concepts.definition: Position within a cycle, in radians. Phase relationships between frequencies determine timbre + localization. Substrate analogue: per-channel temporal alignment in the cochlear nucleus.

concepts.name: wavelength
concepts.definition: Spatial distance of one cycle. λ = c/f where c is sound speed (~343 m/s). Substrate analogue: subsumed by frequency representation.

concepts.name: pitch
concepts.definition: Perceptual correlate of frequency. Categorical (notes) + continuous (siren). Substrate analogue: peak in substrate's tonotopic representation; F0 estimate.

concepts.name: timbre
concepts.definition: What distinguishes a violin from a flute playing the same pitch + loudness. Determined by spectral envelope + temporal envelope + transients. Substrate analogue: the substrate's pattern across multiple gammatone channels simultaneously.

concepts.name: loudness
concepts.definition: Perceptual correlate of amplitude. Sone scale; equal-loudness contours (Fletcher-Munson). Logarithmic. Substrate analogue: integrated power across gammatone bands with frequency-dependent weighting.

concepts.name: duration
concepts.definition: Perceived length of a sound. Cortical integration time ~50-200ms for fine perception. Substrate analogue: substrate's persistent σ activation period.

concepts.name: harmonic
concepts.definition: Integer-multiple frequency of a fundamental. Pure tones at 100, 200, 300 Hz form a harmonic series. Substrate analogue: substrate's harmonic-template matching in pitch perception.

concepts.name: fundamental_frequency
concepts.definition: F0 — lowest periodic component of a complex tone. The pitch we hear. Substrate analogue: substrate's F0 estimate from auditory_cortex.

concepts.name: overtone
concepts.definition: Frequency above F0 in a complex tone. Harmonic overtones are integer multiples; inharmonic ones aren't (bells, drums). Substrate analogue: secondary peaks in substrate's gammatone output.

concepts.name: partial
concepts.definition: Any sinusoidal component of a complex sound, harmonic or not. Substrate analogue: individual gammatone channel output.

concepts.name: formant
concepts.definition: Resonance of a vocal tract — peaks in the spectral envelope of speech. F1 + F2 distinguish vowels. Substrate analogue: substrate's formant detector in phonology Mt.

concepts.name: spectrum
concepts.definition: Frequency-domain representation. Amplitude per frequency at one moment. Substrate analogue: substrate's gammatone output at one tick.

concepts.name: spectrogram
concepts.definition: Time × frequency × amplitude. Visual + computational standard for analysis. Substrate analogue: substrate's auditory cortex input — frequency by tick.

concepts.name: envelope
concepts.definition: Slowly-varying outline of a signal — amplitude over time. Substrate analogue: substrate's per-channel envelope follower.

concepts.name: attack
concepts.definition: ADSR. Time from silence to peak. Distinguishes percussive (fast) from sustained (slow). Substrate analogue: substrate's onset detector in cochlear nucleus.

concepts.name: decay
concepts.definition: ADSR. Time from peak to sustain level. Substrate analogue: substrate's envelope-derivative tracker.

concepts.name: sustain
concepts.definition: ADSR. Steady-state level during note hold. Substrate analogue: substrate's sustained σ level.

concepts.name: release
concepts.definition: ADSR. Time from sustain to silence after note ends. Substrate analogue: substrate's offset-decay rate.

concepts.name: transient
concepts.definition: Brief high-energy onset characterizing percussive + plucked sounds. Critical for instrument identification. Substrate analogue: substrate's high-derivative onset event.

concepts.name: noise
concepts.definition: Aperiodic + irregular signal. White (flat spectrum), pink (1/f), brown (1/f²). Substrate analogue: substrate's high-entropy unstructured input.

concepts.name: tone
concepts.definition: Periodic signal with defined pitch. Pure (sine) or complex (multiple harmonics). Substrate analogue: substrate's peaked gammatone output.

concepts.name: interval
concepts.definition: Distance between two pitches, measured in semitones or ratios. Octave = 2:1, fifth = 3:2, fourth = 4:3. Substrate analogue: relational concept between two pitch detections.

concepts.name: octave
concepts.definition: 12 semitone interval; 2:1 frequency ratio. Pitches an octave apart are heard as the same note class — chroma. Substrate analogue: substrate's modular pitch representation.

concepts.name: semitone
concepts.definition: Smallest interval in 12-TET = factor of 2^(1/12). Substrate analogue: substrate's discrete pitch quantum.

concepts.name: scale
concepts.definition: Ordered set of pitches within an octave. Major, minor, modes, pentatonic. Substrate analogue: substrate's expected-pitch template.

concepts.name: key
concepts.definition: Tonal center; one pitch around which others gravitate. Major or minor mode. Substrate analogue: substrate's basin attractor for melodic prediction.

concepts.name: mode
concepts.definition: Specific pattern of intervals defining a scale. Dorian, Mixolydian, etc. Each has a distinctive flavor. Substrate analogue: substrate's per-context expectation pattern.

concepts.name: melody
concepts.definition: Sequence of pitches over time forming a coherent musical line. Substrate analogue: substrate's pitch-vs-time pattern.

concepts.name: harmony
concepts.definition: Simultaneous sounding of pitches — chords + progression. Substrate analogue: substrate's parallel pattern across pitch detectors.

concepts.name: chord
concepts.definition: Three or more pitches sounding together. Triads, sevenths, extensions. Substrate analogue: substrate's multi-peak gammatone state.

concepts.name: counterpoint
concepts.definition: Multiple independent melodic lines sounding simultaneously. Bach. Substrate analogue: substrate's parallel pitch-tracking.

concepts.name: consonance
concepts.definition: Pitches whose combination sounds stable + pleasant. Simple frequency ratios. Substrate analogue: substrate's low-frustration multi-pitch state.

concepts.name: dissonance
concepts.definition: Pitches whose combination sounds unstable + tense, demanding resolution. Substrate analogue: substrate's high-frustration multi-pitch state.

concepts.name: rhythm
concepts.definition: Pattern of durations + accents over time. Substrate analogue: substrate's temporal pattern of onset events.

concepts.name: beat
concepts.definition: Underlying pulse; the felt regular time-unit. Substrate analogue: substrate's tempo-tracker output.

concepts.name: tempo
concepts.definition: Speed of beats; bpm. Most natural ~120 bpm. Substrate analogue: substrate's clock-rate for music-related cortices.

concepts.name: meter
concepts.definition: Grouping of beats. 4/4 = four beats per bar. Strong + weak accents. Substrate analogue: substrate's higher-order temporal periodicity tracker.

concepts.name: dynamics
concepts.definition: Musical loudness levels. Pianissimo to fortissimo. Expressive variation. Substrate analogue: substrate's amplitude-modulation tracker.

concepts.name: articulation
concepts.definition: How notes are attacked + connected. Staccato vs legato. Substrate analogue: substrate's note-boundary detection.

concepts.name: vibrato
concepts.definition: Periodic frequency modulation, ~5-7 Hz. Vocal + string-instrument expression. Substrate analogue: substrate's frequency-modulation detector.

rules.name: pitch_arises_from_periodicity
rules.head: the substrate detects periodic structure in audio input
rules.body: the period maps to a pitch via F0 estimation; the inverse of period in Hz is the pitch. Substrate's fundamental-frequency pipeline.

rules.name: timbre_emerges_from_spectral_pattern
rules.head: two sounds have the same pitch but differ in instrument or vowel
rules.body: they differ in spectral envelope across gammatone channels. Substrate's timbre representation = multi-channel pattern, not a single value.

rules.name: consonance_is_simple_frequency_ratios
rules.head: two pitches sound together in simple integer ratios (2:1, 3:2)
rules.body: the substrate computes low frustration / high coherence between their gammatone representations. Helmholtz 1863. Substrate's consonance detector.

rules.name: beat_induction_from_temporal_pattern
rules.head: the substrate hears a repeated rhythmic pattern
rules.body: it extracts an underlying beat — the most parsimonious periodicity that fits the events. Large + Kolen 1994. Substrate's beat-tracking via temporal expectation.

rules.name: tonal_hierarchy_emerges_from_exposure
rules.head: the substrate has heard much music in a given key
rules.body: it develops a hierarchy: tonic > dominant > mediant > others. Krumhansl 1990. Substrate's per-key basin landscape.

rules.name: expectation_drives_musical_emotion
rules.head: the substrate hears music violating or fulfilling expectations
rules.body: the prediction error drives emotional response. Huron 2006 — substrate's coherence-drive on musical predictions.
